nodes.summary: Let $m, k$ be natural numbers and let $c$ send every clause $j < m$ to a diamond $c(j) < k$. For each diamond $i$, list the clauses $j < m$ with $c(j) = i$ in increasing order (the clause vertices picked up by the row of diamond $i$). Concatenating these lists for $i = 0, \dots, k - 1$ gives a permutation of $0, 1, \dots, m - 1$.
nodes.title: Each clause is picked up by exactly one row

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $t$, let $T_i = m + i(3m+2)$. Concatenating, for $i = 0, \dots, t - 1$, the lists $T_i, T_i + 1, \dots, T_i + 3m + 1$ of $3m + 2$ consecutive numbers (the top and the row of diamond $i$) gives the list $m, m + 1, \dots, m + t(3m+2) - 1$, that is, the numbers from $m$ to $T_t - 1$ in increasing order.
nodes.title: The first $t$ diamonds occupy consecutive vertices

nodes.summary: For $m$ clauses, a diamond $i$ and any clause-to-diamond map $c$, the row of diamond $i$ read left to right, with the clauses sent to $i$ by $c$ inserted, starts at its left end, the row vertex $T_i + 1$, where $T_i = m + i(3m+2)$ is the top of diamond $i$.
nodes.title: A row starts at its left end

nodes.summary: For $m$ clauses, a diamond $i$, a clause-to-diamond map $c$ and a direction $b$, let $T_i = m + i(3m+2)$ be the top of diamond $i$. The visit of diamond $i$ in direction $b$ is a rearrangement of the list that consists of $T_i, T_i + 1, \dots, T_i + 3m + 1$ and then the clauses $j < m$ with $c(j) = i$ in increasing order.
nodes.title: A diamond visit is a block of consecutive vertices plus its clauses

nodes.summary: For $m$ clauses, a diamond $i$, a clause-to-diamond map $c$ and a direction $b$, the visit of diamond $i$ is the list consisting of its top $T_i = m + i(3m+2)$ followed by its row with the clauses sent to $i$ by $c$ inserted, read left to right if $b$ is true and right to left otherwise.
nodes.title: The visit of a diamond

nodes.summary: Let $m, k$ be natural numbers, let $c$ send every clause $j < m$ to a diamond $c(j) < k$, let $d$ be any directions, and let $T_k = m + k(3m+2)$. The forward path through the first $k$ diamonds in directions $d$ with clause choice $c$ is a permutation of the list $0, 1, \dots, T_k$.
nodes.title: The forward path visits every vertex once

nodes.title: The forward path through the diamonds

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $i$ and a map $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the clauses picked up by diamond $i$ are the list of all $j < m$ with $c(j) = i$, in increasing order.
nodes.title: Clauses picked up by a diamond

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $i$ and a map $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $r = m + i(3m + 2) + 1$ be the left end of the row of diamond $i$. The row of diamond $i$ for $c$ (with its clause vertices inserted) is a permutation of the concatenation of the list $r, r + 1, \dots, r + 3m$ and the list of clauses picked up by diamond $i$ for $c$, that is, of all $j < m$ with $c(j) = i$ in increasing order.
nodes.title: The vertices of a diamond row

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $i$ be natural numbers and $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ a map, and write $r_l = m + i(3m + 2) + 1 + l$ for the row vertices of diamond $i$. The row of diamond $i$ for $c$ is the list $r_0, r_1, \dots, r_{3m}$ in which, for every $j < m$ with $c(j) = i$, the clause vertex $j$ is inserted right after $r_{3j+1}$.
nodes.title: The row of a diamond with its clauses inserted

nodes.title: Chain condition for a diamond row

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $i$ be natural numbers and let $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. A natural number $v$ is one of the clause vertices picked up by the row of diamond $i$ under $c$, for $m$ clauses, if and only if $v < m$ and $c(v) = i$.

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$, $i$ and every function $c : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the list of clause vertices picked up by the row of diamond $i$ under $c$, for $m$ clauses, has no repeated entries.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
